how: Quasar moonsaults off the top of the steel cage onto Tony for the pin.

title: iwf-icehomepage-1996-universal
label: Ricky "Top Gun" Santana

won.source: Held as of the fed's own 13 February 1997 broadcast, which calls the belt the 'Universal Heavyweight' Championship (a fuller form of this title's own registered name); no won-date survives in the held record. Supersedes American Ninja's own still-champion-at-record-end reign of December 1996 with no attested title change in between.

note: Successfully defends the belt against I-Roc Titan, 12 February 1997, after Concrete strikes I-Roc with a chair.

title: iwf-icehomepage-1996-united-states
label: 'All American' Atlas

won.source: Held as of the fed's own 13 February 1997 broadcast; no won-date survives in the held record. Supersedes Amish Warrior's own still-champion-at-record-end reign of December 1996 with no attested title change in between.

note: Retains the title in a lumberjack match against Flawed to Perfection, ruled a no contest on 12 February 1997 when members of three rival stables brawl to ringside.

title: iwf-icehomepage-1996-television
label: Butterball

won.source: Held as of the fed's own 13 February 1997 broadcast. The title was vacant per the held record's 12 December 1996 broadcast, pending a sealed steel-cage match at that year's Christmas Day pay-per-view; no document surviving in the held record confirms that match's result, so no won-date is claimed.

note: Defends the newly-filled title against Darlock on 13 February 1997 and again against Sao on 19 February 1997 at the War of the Alliances.

title: iwf-icehomepage-1996-us-tag-team
label: Death & Destruction

won.source: Held as of the fed's own 13 February 1997 broadcast; no won-date survives in the held record, and no earlier attestation of this title exists in the held record.

note: A non-title outing against Flying Thunder is previewed for that same night.

title: iwf-icehomepage-1996-television-tag-team
label: Assault & Battery

won.source: Held as of the fed's own 13 February 1997 broadcast; no won-date survives in the held record. Supersedes Flying Thunder's own still-champion-at-record-end reign of 12 December 1996 (id iwf-1996-12-television-tag-team-r002) with no attested title change in between -- that reign's own end_how should be revisited against this row when both are merged.

note: Previewed defending the title against the Apocalypse at the War of the Alliances, 19 February 1997.
